subject: CloudFlux: recommended GPU sprint signals & next steps
messages:
From: Ameet Shah <ameet@cloudflux.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask: upcoming Q4 ramp (CloudFlux)

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As CloudFlux ramps towards a Q4 launch window (targeting GA in late Oct), procurement asked us for a recommended committed capacity profile they can include in the SOW. I've attached our internal pipeline export for the next six months. High level asks:

- We need a recommended minimum reserved GPU pool (weekly cadence) to keep latency under 120ms for the initial 50k monthly active users projection.
- Estimate of burst credits for predictable spikes during weekly model retrains.
- Any cost levers (quantization, batching) we should propose to procurement so they can compare reserved vs burst economics.

Could your team provide a first pass by early next week? Procurement looped in a general mailbox in case we need a PO template.

Attachments: CloudFlux_pipeline_export.csv (CSV, 18KB)

Best,
Ameet
Ameet Shah
Head of AI Products, CloudFlux
ameet@cloudflux.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ameet Shah <ameet@cloudflux.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: upcoming Q4 ramp (CloudFlux)

Ameet — thanks for the pipeline export, that's helpful. Looping infra and finance so we can surface an actionable "sprint signal" you can include in the SOW. High-level plan below; I'll produce a spreadsheet with week-by-week numbers (attached).

Summary recommendation (first pass):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for the first 8 weeks post-GA, scaled to 12 during weekly retrain windows.
- Burst credits: 4x weekly burst slots (ephemeral) to cover traffic spikes during feature launches.
- Cost options: recommend 16-bit quant + batching at 64 tokens to preserve latency and cut token cost ~35%; alternate option with 8-bit Q4 for additional savings if model quality is validated.

Requests for internal reviewers:
- Laura — confirm whether 8->12 mapping is feasible from a sales/commitment perspective (pricing cadence).
- Ben — can finance draft a simple reserved vs burst comparison we can share with procurement (include DocuSign cadence)?
- Karthik — confirm infra constraints for the proposed mapping and whether there are regional placement considerations.

I'm attaching the working file (initial-sprint-signal-v1.xlsx). If we agree, I'll turn this into a one-pager for CloudFlux procurement.

[Attachment: initial-sprint-signal-v1.xlsx]

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: upcoming Q4 ramp (CloudFlux)

Tessa / team — quick infra reality check after looking at the worksheet. A few notes: 

- Baseline mapping (8->12) is plausible in us-west with current pool capacity, but only if we reserve the fleet early (3-4 week lead for GPU procurement/pool assignment). If they want a firm SLA in the SOW for week-of-Oct-22, we need to lock commits by Sept 1.
- We can shave ~20% off committed GPUs with two mitigations: aggressive KV-prefix caching (good for our use case if inputs are repetitive) and a 4x batching factor on retrain days. That requires a short validation run to ensure tail latency stays beneath 180ms under load.
- Regional note: if CloudFlux requires multi-region redundancy (us-west + eu-west), add a +30% safety margin to the pool.

Action items for me: I'll run a quick simulation using last-quarter traffic profiles and push updated numbers by Tue EOD. Also flagging that the burst-credit mechanism will need a temporary quota bump for the initial 6 weeks.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: upcoming Q4 ramp (CloudFlux)

Quick finance read —

- Reserved vs burst economics: for the 8 GPU baseline the committed unit price (12-month) nets ~28% cost reduction vs on-demand. If CloudFlux prefers a shorter 6-month ramp we can do a blended pricing option (6-month reserve + burst credits) but it will only yield ~12% savings.
- If they accept 8->12 with a 12-month commit we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 0.5 GPU-months) to help offset migration/testing. I'll draft the pricing language for the SOW and put it into DocuSign for signature.

DocuSign link (draft): https://www.docusign.net/contract/CFX-1893-sign

Laura — advise if we should also surface a quarterly true-up clause vs a linear commit.

Ben
Ben Carter
Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ameet Shah <ameet@cloudflux.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: upcoming Q4 ramp (CloudFlux)

Ameet — circling back with a consolidated recommendation and next steps:

1) Recommendation (finalized first pass):
   - Reserve: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs baseline; scale to 12 for weekly retrain windows (first 8 weeks post-GA).
   - Burst: 4 ephemeral burst slots for weekly peaks (automated quota bump for initial 6 weeks).
   - Pricing: 12-month committed pricing preferred (approx -28% vs on-demand). Option for blended 6-month reserve + burst (approx -12% savings).

2) Risk & mitigations:
   - If multi-region redundancy required, add +30% to pool (infra flagged).
   - We recommend a short validation run (48 hours) using your top-50 request patterns to confirm tail latency under 4x batching.

3) Next steps / mutual action items:
   - Tessa: convert this into a one-page SOW appendix and send to procurement (target Thu EOD).
   - Ben: finalize DocuSign pricing draft and onboarding credit (in progress).
   - Karthik: run the traffic simulation and confirm quota bump timeline (due Tue EOD).
   - CloudFlux (Ameet): confirm whether multi-region redundancy is required and whether procurement wants a 6- or 12-month commit window.

Attachments included: initial-sprint-signal-v1.xlsx, CloudFlux_SLA-request.pdf

If that all looks good, let's schedule a 30-minute handoff with procurement early next week.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial-sprint-signal-v1.xlsx]
[Attachment: CloudFlux_SLA-request.pdf]
